_purpose: Fallback painting catalog for the automated content pipeline. Built 2026-08-10 after discovering the cloud routine's sandbox environment blocks network egress to wholeheartedarts.com (EGRESS_BLOCKED/403), which silently killed the 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-10 scheduled runs before they could pick a painting. The routine should read this file instead of live-fetching the site. This is a workaround, not a permanent fix — see 'staleness_warning' below.
staleness_warning: This catalog is a point-in-time snapshot (2026-08-10). Prices, availability (sold/in-stock), and the painting list itself can drift from the live site over time. If a routine run using this catalog picks a painting that's since sold or changed price, that's an acceptable known risk versus not running at all — but this file should be refreshed periodically (ask Claude to re-fetch and update it), and ideally retired entirely once wholeheartedarts.com is added to the sandbox environment's egress allowlist (the proper fix — see .claude/skills/publishing-handoff/SKILL.md and CLAUDE.md workflow notes).
selection_note: Atelier and Studio collections are EQUALLY weighted — do not default to Atelier over Studio or vice versa. Both are fully detailed below at the same level of depth. Pick whichever painting best fits the topic/angle for this run, from either collection.

atelier_collection_unused.title: Whimsical Gdansk
atelier_collection_unused.medium: Mixed media (fabric, paint, metallic accents, raised texture)
atelier_collection_unused.description: A small yet intricately detailed work celebrating memory, place, and imagination. Inspired by Gdansk's colorful architecture and historical charm, the piece evokes 'a little city glowing after dusk — full of crooked rooftops, golden windows, tiny flags, textured walls, and hidden stories.' Invites viewers to 'pause, look closer, and step into a place where history, childhood memory, travel, faith, and imagination meet.'

atelier_collection_unused.title: Gathered Light
atelier_collection_unused.medium: Mixed media (collage, paint, handwritten marks, and line work)
atelier_collection_unused.description: Original mixed media portrait featuring layered fragments of pattern, texture, handwritten marks, and luminous color. Explores tension between fragility and resilience, with a face emerging softly through complexity, memory, and movement. Reflects 'the beauty of becoming: how light still finds us in unfinished places.'

atelier_collection_unused.title: Guided by Grace
atelier_collection_unused.description: Structural mixed media piece capturing resilience and divine guidance through vibrant colors and textures. Psalm 34 text is integrated into highlighted areas, emphasizing God's goodness guiding our path. An illuminated figure symbolizes hope and strength amid challenges. 'A reminder of the uplifting power of faith and the beauty found in trusting the journey.' Free domestic shipping (mainland US); local pickup available.

atelier_collection_unused.title: Cleansing Waters - Divided by Grace
atelier_collection_unused.description: Abstract painting divided into two realms. Above, a crowd stained with red symbolizes the burdens of sin and emotional turmoil. Below, figures gathered around a well of living water are portrayed in white, radiating purity and renewal. Vibrant blues evoke hope, contrasting the heaviness above. Illustrates 'the journey from darkness to light, inviting reflection on redemption and transformation.'
atelier_collection_unused.availability_note: Black frame in stock now; white frame option available for shipping/pickup after Jan 4 (per site copy at time of fetch — treat as approximate/possibly stale).

atelier_collection_unused.title: Guardian of Innocence
atelier_collection_unused.description: Explores maternal protection and sacred love: 'a mother rests with her child, eyes closed, not in weariness, but in trust.' Addresses protection without fear, guardianship aware of its own limits yet committed to love. Layers color and texture to suggest 'a life shaped through both breaking and beauty — nothing wasted, everything held.' Rich layered detail 'reveals itself slowly — inviting stillness, reflection, and reverence.'

atelier_collection_unused.title: Patience
atelier_collection_unused.description: A quiet yet powerful presence, blending layered texture, soft movement, and luminous circular forms around a contemplative figure. Speaks of 'inner stillness, endurance, and the kind of patience that is formed slowly — through waiting, reflection, and trust.'
atelier_collection_unused.note: Not the same as the $400 'Patience' piece in the Origins collection — this is the Atelier piece.

atelier_collection_unused.title: Awakened Fields
atelier_collection_unused.description: 'Not every beautiful thing is gentle. Some beauty asks you to stay and look longer.' Wild, watchful, full of life — for the collector drawn to texture, meaning, and bold presence.

atelier_collection_unused.title: Heaven Declares
atelier_collection_unused.medium: Mixed media (fabric, paper, and acrylic on canvas)
atelier_collection_unused.description: Inspired by Psalm 19, exploring how divine truth brings salvation to the heart. A central figure constructed from Scripture fragments sits amid color and texture suggesting surrender and joy. Intentionally rough paper and fabric edges convey: 'We are created beautifully, yet we move through this life marked by weakness, process, and imperfection. We are, in many ways, perfectly imperfect.' Balances Psalm 19's dual revelation — God's glory in creation and mercy in His Word.
atelier_collection_unused.caution_note: Also based on Psalm 19, same as topic 004 (Psalm of the Birch Forest). Angle is different (Scripture-fragment figure vs. birch trunks), so still usable, but a writer should differentiate the framing clearly from 004 rather than repeating the same scripture-quote-and-angle.

atelier_collection_unused.title: Love Eternal Rhapsody
atelier_collection_unused.medium: Mixed media — fabric, paper, acrylic, metal, gold and silver flakes
atelier_collection_unused.description: Depicts 'a man and woman who exude the elegance of a royal couple on their wedding day,' evoking a fairy-tale feeling. Incorporates scripture from Colossians 3 and marriage blessings. 'It starts with the first kiss.' Reflects 'the richness and complexity of life and love,' with spiritual elements discreetly woven throughout. Delivery/shipping included in price.

atelier_collection_unused.title: They Will Call Me Blessed
atelier_collection_unused.description: Draws inspiration from Luke 1:46-54 (Mary's Magnificat). Richly layered texture combining fabric and acrylic on a custom-constructed support using salvaged materials. Linen stretched by the artist on a recycled wood frame and heavy linen curtain.

atelier_collection_unused.title: Never Stop Wonder
atelier_collection_unused.description: Vibrant abstract piece with 'layers of vivid florals, playful marks, soft scribbles, and unexpected bursts of light' across a dark background with reds, turquoise, yellows, pinks, and greens. Evokes 'a garden of imagination, where flowers, stars, seeds, birds, and hidden symbols all speak in their own quiet language.' Celebrates how 'even in a complicated world, the heart can remain open' to meaning and discovery.

atelier_collection_unused.title: Messenger
atelier_collection_unused.medium: Structural acrylic painting on canvas with mixed media
atelier_collection_unused.description: Presents 'a solitary bird set within a richly layered abstract landscape.' Textural, expressive, gently luminous. Engages themes of intuition and reflection through symbolic visual language. 'For the collector who is drawn to symbolism, texture, and quiet emotional depth, Messenger offers a presence that feels both grounding and mysterious.' Restored gold and green wooden frame included.

atelier_collection_unused.title: Wisdom of Mothers
atelier_collection_unused.medium: Mixed media — fabric, paper, and acrylic
atelier_collection_unused.description: Inspired by Proverbs 31, honoring 'the quiet strength, sacrifice, protection, and spiritual covering carried by women across generations.' Figures in layered red, rose, gold, and earthy tones, garments incorporating texture, pattern, and Scripture passages. White expressive lines suggest 'shelter, struggle, and divine covering.' 'A tribute to feminine strength rooted in faith, love, and holy endurance.' Black metal frame, wall-ready, included in price.

atelier_collection_excluded.reason: Sold out per site at time of fetch (2026-08-10) — verify before use, do not post about unavailable work as if purchasable.

studio_collection_unused.title: Carrying Burden, Seeking Light
studio_collection_unused.medium: Mixed media on canvas: acrylic and pastel oil
studio_collection_unused.description: Two intertwined figures in blue form an intimate embrace, suggesting 'grief, memory, love, and protection all held in the same body.' One appears to support the other, with warmth from rust, copper, rose, and golden accents that 'rise like light breaking through hardship.' Deliberate tension between 'burden and devotion, struggle and warmth, heaviness and illumination.' 'This piece is for the collector who understands that love is not always light — sometimes love is carrying, holding, staying, and still searching for the light together.'

studio_collection_unused.title: The Time of Singing Has Come
studio_collection_unused.description: Painted red poppies, fragments of music, patterned papers, texture, handwritten words, and a Scripture reference convey 'the feeling of creation waking again.' Inspired by the artist's Polish heritage and Song of Songs 2:12: 'What was quiet begins to bloom. What was hidden begins to appear.' Explores joy 'that comes after waiting.'

studio_collection_unused.title: The Lord is My Light
studio_collection_unused.medium: Textured paint, layered surface detail, handwritten scripture-inspired text, shimmer finish
studio_collection_unused.description: A golden sunflower with layered texture and shimmer opens toward light. Handwritten words reading 'The Lord is my light and salvation' encircle the bloom. Black circular frame with sparkling detail. 'A small altar of hope for the home.'

studio_collection_unused.title: After the Rain, the Windows Kept Glowing
studio_collection_unused.medium: Paint, collage/textile-like elements, layered texture, glossy finish
studio_collection_unused.description: A small urban scene evoking 'a remembered evening — wet streets, tilted rooftops, glowing windows, and the quiet shimmer of rain moving through the air.' Layered paint, fabric-like collage elements, deep rooflines, jewel-like reflections. Conveys 'a sense of shelter, weather, and home.' Framed in a natural wood frame.

studio_collection_unused.title: Quiet Abundance
studio_collection_unused.medium: Mixed media on wooden canvas board
studio_collection_unused.description: A bouquet of hydrangeas resting in a warm terracotta vessel, surrounded by luminous golds, soft lavender, and layered notes of violet, blush, and sky blue. 'A tender celebration of beauty in its quietest form.' For 'someone drawn to softness, poetry, and the quiet emotional language of flowers.'

studio_collection_unused.title: The Center Holds
studio_collection_unused.description: Layered color, fine hand-drawn detail, and a radiant floral center on a luminous yellow-green ground. Spirals, leaves, dots, and textured marks surround it with 'a sense of growth and protection.' Well-suited for emerging collectors and designers seeking 'a small work with warmth, color, and personal character.'

studio_collection_unused.title: Held in the Heights
studio_collection_unused.description: 'Some places look rugged until the light touches them. Then you realize they were never empty. Only holy in a quieter way.' For the collector 'who loves depth, beauty, and the gentle reminder that even high and hidden places can hold grace.'

studio_collection_unused.title: A Field Full of Yes
studio_collection_unused.description: 'A joyful meadow-inspired piece filled with color, movement, and light' — layered greens, soft sky tones, pinks, reds, yellows, blues, and delicate floral details. 'Smaller in size, but rich in texture, energy, and tiny discoveries up close.' 'A fresh, uplifting piece with a peaceful but playful presence.'

studio_collection_unused.title: The Spiral of Time
studio_collection_unused.medium: Richly textured acrylic on canvas, framed in black
studio_collection_unused.description: Exploring the layered dance of past, presence, and future. Rich circular movement, luminous blues, soft ivory, gold, and rose tones gather toward a quiet center — 'contemplative and alive.' Deep texture gives the painting dimension and a refined presence.

studio_collection_unused.title: The Key Within
studio_collection_unused.description: Inspired by Viktor Frankl's *Man's Search for Meaning*. A solitary figure stands before a barred opening amid layered texture, warm earth tones, fractured marks, and traces of light. A small key at the figure's head symbolizes inner reserves — courage, grace, dignity, hope that persists 'even when the world feels closed off.' Frankl: 'When we are no longer able to change a situation, we are challenged to change ourselves.' Part of the 'Where Memory and Meaning Meet' pairing with 'Where the Walls Remember.'
studio_collection_unused.caution_note: Paired thematically with 'Where the Walls Remember' (Holocaust/Auschwitz remembrance, see below) via Frankl's Holocaust-survivor authorship — this piece itself is about resilience/meaning generally, lower sensitivity than its pair, but a writer should decide independently whether to name Frankl's own history explicitly or keep the frame general.

studio_collection_unused.title: Where the Walls Remember
studio_collection_unused.description: 'A visual memorial — not only to the victims of Auschwitz, but to every life marked by cruelty, silence, and loss.' A red field carries symbolic weight; layered forms suggest figures that 'rise and remain: quiet witnesses, fragile yet unerased.' Anchored by the phrase 'We Will Not Forget.' Addresses remembrance, endurance, and 'the sacred duty to keep human dignity alive in the face of evil.'
studio_collection_unused.caution_note: NEEDS HUMAN DECISION if ever selected: this piece explicitly memorializes Auschwitz/the Holocaust. That is a real, sensitive historical subject requiring careful, respectful, non-trivializing treatment — not a subject for the unattended automated pipeline to write about without human review, given how much judgment post 003's much lighter tragedy-reference already required from Agata directly. Recommend excluding this piece from automated/unattended selection; flag it for Agata to write or closely direct herself if she wants it covered.

studio_collection_unused.title: Her Quiet Knowing of Grace
studio_collection_unused.description: A gentle mixed media portrait on paper — soft layers, expressive marks, a quiet gaze 'both tender and strong.' Speaks of 'inner blessing — the kind that does not need to announce itself, but rests deeply within.' Framed behind plexiglass.

studio_collection_unused.title: Where Grace Settles
studio_collection_unused.description: 'Soft blues, earthen reds, golds, greens, and gentle pinks come together like a landscape after waiting — tender, unsettled, and still full of light.' 'Grace often comes gently. It settles over the low places, the unfinished places, the places still becoming.'
studio_collection_unused.price_note: Site listing showed $475 in the collection index but $675 on the product page itself at time of fetch — verify current price before posting.

studio_collection_unused.title: What Grace Grows
studio_collection_unused.description: A luminous floral original — large expressive blooms in pink, lavender, blue, green, and golden yellow. 'Carries both energy and gentleness — bright, but peaceful; expressive, but deeply feminine.' Brings 'hope, abundance, and quiet praise into a room.'
studio_collection_unused.availability_note: Not framed — additional mixed media details may be added before framing, per site copy.

studio_collection_unused.title: What the Body Remembers
studio_collection_unused.medium: Original mixed media painting on canvas
studio_collection_unused.description: Layered abstract composition in warm rose, clay, weathered gold, and muted earth tones, with delicate linear markings resembling 'fragments of an ancient language.' Shifts visually through the day as light interacts with its textured surface. Created 'to evoke feeling rather than explanation' — 'softness, memory, and the quiet architecture we carry beneath the surface.'

studio_collection_unused.title: Unexpected Happiness
studio_collection_unused.description: A 'happy explosion' of vibrant, colorful acrylic work — undeserved yet joyful. Represents a refusal to accept failure's grey reality, transforming into unexpected joy. Black frame with white mat.

studio_collection_unused.title: Sunshine Filled Hearts - Set of 2
studio_collection_unused.description: Two paintings meant for display together, each with radiant yellow sunflowers against lush green backdrops. Fabric integration for tactile richness, luminous acrylic layers. Each incorporates verses from 1 Corinthians 13:3-8a woven throughout, on themes of love, patience, and kindness.

studio_collection_unused.title: All the Love We Need
studio_collection_unused.description: Repeated words, handwritten marks, bright hearts, and energetic color create an impression of love declared repeatedly. Balances 'spontaneous and expressive' with intentional design: 'love is not always quiet or polished.' Bold palette, 'warmth, joy, and a sense of lighthearted abundance.'

studio_collection_unused.title: Divine in the Sky
studio_collection_unused.medium: Mixed media (fabric, acrylic, alcohol ink, gold leaf)
studio_collection_unused.description: A sunset painting capturing the divine nature and splendor of the sky at sunrise and sunset. Romans 1:20 is written into the horizon. 'A testament to the glory of creation.' Signed with Certificate of Authenticity included.

studio_collection_unused.title: Finding Light in the Darkness #2
studio_collection_unused.medium: Mixed media on canvas board: acrylic, fabric, markers
studio_collection_unused.description: Incorporates Psalm 119:75-77 as a spiritual anchor during difficult times. Described by the artist as 'a meditative and prayerful experience.' Suitable for personal spaces or as a gift, meant to remind that 'there is always hope and light to be found in Christ' amid suffering.

studio_collection_unused.title: Love Her Like Yourself
studio_collection_unused.description: Inspired by Genesis 2:21-24 (ESV) — the creation of woman from man's rib, 'one flesh.' Words written directly into the composition.
studio_collection_unused.availability_note: Per site copy at time of fetch: available for pickup, or ships/delivers after an exhibition at Chambers Walk ends Sept 1 — verify this is still accurate before use, likely stale by the time this catalog is read.

studio_collection_unused.title: Imagine
studio_collection_unused.description: Invites viewers to contemplate 'the world where people understood the difference between want and need, freedom and chaos, love and self-indulgent, differences and commonalities' — a spiritual call to responsible stewardship rather than indulgence.

studio_collection_unused.title: Wholehearted Pasture
studio_collection_unused.description: John 13:5 scripture written into the sky as an integrated element of the composition.

studio_collection_unused.title: Prayerful Mother - Psalm 139
studio_collection_unused.medium: Acrylic painting with words of Psalm 139
studio_collection_unused.description: 'A prayer for a mom and a child.' Explores the wonder and worry of pregnancy — 'we all were uniquely made by God on our mothers womb.' Reminds parents 'he has a good plan. All is written in his book.' Grey wood frame.

studio_collection_unused.title: Breaking the Chains
studio_collection_unused.description: No description text published on the product page beyond the title itself — treat as a thin-narrative piece; write a shorter, more image-led post if selected rather than inventing meaning.

studio_collection_unused.title: In the Blossom
studio_collection_unused.description: Inspired by the Polish tale of Thumbelina, born from a flower blossom — imaginative musings about sleeping within a flower's protective embrace. Evolves into a meditation on spiritual renewal: 'we are ultimately reborn by the Spirit of God, but before that the seed must fall on the good soil,' with imagery of seeds flourishing in fertile ground vs. perishing among rocks and weeds.

studio_collection_unused.title: Where She Cried Flower Grew
studio_collection_unused.medium: Mixed media on canvas, structural painting knife technique
studio_collection_unused.description: Reflects on maternal resilience: 'Mothers tears are never wasted. As mothers we are committed to a better future for our children.' Maternal tears as 'a powerful tool of change regardless their geographical location or skin color.'

studio_collection_unused.title: Red
studio_collection_unused.description: No narrative text published beyond technical specs — thin-narrative piece, write shorter/image-led if selected rather than inventing meaning.

studio_collection_unused.title: In Plain Sight
studio_collection_unused.description: Part of the 'Heart of Healing' original series. No further narrative text published beyond that on the product page — thin-narrative, write shorter/image-led if selected.
studio_collection_unused.note: Different piece from the same-titled $500 painting also listed in the Origins collection — this is the Studio piece.

studio_collection_unused.title: Held by the Word - Be Still and Know that I am God
studio_collection_unused.description: Layered color, texture, movement, and softness, with scripture from Psalm 37 woven into the background. 'Reflective, peaceful, almost wrapped in that truth. Not untouched by life, but held through it.' On 'truth being hidden in plain sight.'

studio_collection_unused.title: United in Prayer
studio_collection_unused.medium: Fabric, paper, and acrylics with clear top coat
studio_collection_unused.description: 'Until the Lord build the house…' (Psalm 127) — a unique interpretation combining a prayer of parents that God will bless their house, prayers for their child, and 'my prayer for all families.' Signed by the artist.

studio_collection_unused.title: Silent, I held my Peace
studio_collection_unused.description: No description or artist narrative published on the product page beyond title and price — thinnest-narrative piece in this catalog. If selected, keep the post very short and image-led; do not invent meaning. Consider contacting Agata for context before using, since the title itself ('Silent, I held my peace') suggests personal weight not explained on the page.

studio_collection_unused.title: Sisters
studio_collection_unused.description: A layered mixed-media portrait exploring closeness, memory, contrast, and the complexity of being known by another person. Two distinct faces bound together by color, movement, and shared atmosphere — one still and intense, the other lower and partially hidden. Speaks to sisterhood's mysteries: how sisters 'mirror, wound, remember, protect, misunderstand, and love one another across time.' Artist experimented with tweezers (usually for broken glass) as an improvised painting tool: 'taking a chance and experimenting pays back.'
studio_collection_unused.caution_note: Agata already posted about this piece herself directly on Instagram/Facebook (organic, not via this pipeline) on 2026-08-09, with her own caption about sisterhood and an anecdote about painting with tweezers. If selected here, take a clearly different angle (this catalog description gives a fuller/different reading than her organic caption did) rather than duplicating her own post.
